view.description: Which compact form this answer is. Absent on a `--full` answer.

questsTotal.description: §3.13: how many quests the registry holds, whichever view was asked for.

quests.description: The compact rows. Present in every view but `--full`.

completedCount.description: `--open` only: how many accepted quests are already finished.

completedIndices.description: `--open` only: their indices, bare — a finished quest's objectives carry no counters at all (SPEC §4.1 quirk 9), so there is nothing else to say about them cheaply.

accepted.description: RETAINED, REDUNDANT, `--full` only: every registry row carries the same acceptance facts, and more. Kept so `--full` answers stay shape-compatible with consumers written against earlier versions.

Quests.description: Two shapes under one contract (§3.13). `--full` carries the uncompacted registry form (`registry`, with the retained-redundant `accepted` list beside it); every other view carries `quests` — one compact row per quest, no prose — plus the view name and the registry total. Exactly one of `registry` / `quests` is present in any answer.

rewards.description: §3.12 (enrich): what completing the quest pays, one row per raw reward allo with the pinned client's interpretation beside it. Readable BEFORE acceptance — the registry holds it.

requirements.description: §3.13 (0.5.0): every requirement with its own status, on the `--full` form.

QuestAccountState.description: Where one account stands on one quest, served as the facts that discriminate it rather than as a single label. The four combinations are exhaustive and mutually exclusive, so any consumer vocabulary maps on without loss: !accepted = never accepted; accepted && complete = already finished; accepted && !complete && objectivesMet = unfinished with the work done; accepted && !complete && !objectivesMet = unfinished with work outstanding. requirementsMet answers whether a quest not yet accepted can be accepted at all.

objectivesMet.description: This layer's evaluation of the objectives it can read — NOT a promise that the finishing transaction will succeed. A consumer needing that guarantee must have the chain simulate the act. The field is not named 'completable' for exactly this reason.

objectives.description: Present only for accepted quests. Accrual objectives count from a snapshot taken at acceptance; before acceptance no snapshot exists and the comparison would run against zero, reading an account's lifetime total as if it were progress. Serving that would hand out a number the world does not hold, so unaccepted rows carry thresholds without progress.

current.description: Progress on the basis named below. Absent where there is nothing to count (boolean objectives) and for a finished quest, whose objectives stop being evaluated. No number is synthesized in either case.

basis.description: since-acceptance = accrual counted from the moment of acceptance, not a balance: spending what you accrued does not un-count it, and a balance held before acceptance does not count toward it. current = the present value (a balance, a level, a score). boolean = met or not, with nothing to count. unknown = a handler this version does not evaluate.

item.description: §3.12 (enrich): present only for target type ITEM — the one item-shaped target the pinned client resolves against the item registry itself (getFromDescription). Types like ITEM_BURN or CRAFT_ITEM carry an index this pin never interprets, and the item and room index spaces overlap, so resolving them would risk a plausible wrong name.

room.description: §3.12 (enrich): present only for target type ROOM — the client's own room lookup. Name only; the description is one room read away.

AlloText.description: The pinned client's own interpretation of one allocation, projected to {name, description}. `image` is never served: two shapes files carry the module NAMESPACE of a png import there rather than a URL (SPEC §4.1 quirk 2).

AlloOut.description: One RAW allocation the world stores (type, index, value) with the pinned client's interpretation of it beside it. Grouped per raw allo deliberately: the interpreter fans out — a BONUS allo yields one entry per bonus, a droptable allo one consolidated entry — so a flat parsed list would have no positional correspondence to what the world holds. `entries` is empty when this pin interprets the shape not at all; the raw facts still stand.

RoomRef.description: §3.12 (enrich): a room index resolved to its registry name and description. Present only when the daemon runs with enrich=true. An index the mirror has no room for keeps the index and answers with empty strings.

QuestRequirement.description: §3.13 (0.5.0): one requirement with its own status. parseQuestRequirements computes this for EVERY requirement and the 0.4.0 surface read only the conjunction, so "requirementsMet: false" never named which requirement failed and a reader could only guess. No pre-acceptance hazard arises here, and that is a fact about the pin rather than an assumption: every quest requirement at this pin uses a BOOL_IS or CURR_MIN handler — there is no accrual handler on any requirement, so there is no acceptance snapshot for a number to be measured against.

current.description: Served exactly where the world holds it and nowhere else — the same no-synthesis rule objectives follow (§1.1).

text.description: The pinned client's own words for the condition (parseConditionalText), verbatim — e.g. "Complete Quest [Ringing Any Bells III]".

QuestRow.description: One row of a COMPACT quests answer (§3.13). Which fields are present depends on the view; index and name are always there, and prose never is.

objectivesMet.description: This layer's evaluation of the objectives it can read — NOT a promise that the finishing transaction will succeed.

unmetRequirements.description: Present ONLY on rows whose requirements are not met, and carrying only the requirements that actually fail: a refusal must name its cause (§3.11).

objectives.description: Present on the accepted/open views and on keyed detail. Never on an unaccepted row: accrual objectives count from a snapshot taken at acceptance, and before acceptance no snapshot exists (§1.1).

description.description: Keyed detail only. Quest description is DIALOGUE — 85 KB of the 141 KB account-form answer measured at one pin, byte for byte the same on every call — so it is never on a listing row (§3.13).

requirements.description: Keyed detail only: every requirement, met or not.
